title: Szerintem X, mert Y: Justifying an Opinion

sections.title: Putting the whole unit together
sections.content: You already know mert ("because") for giving a reason, and you already know szerintem, azt hiszem, and gondolom for opening an opinion. Chain them together — opinion first, then mert, then your reason — and you have a complete, convincing sentence: give your view, then immediately back it up.

sections.title: Opinion + reason
rows: In my opinion X, because Y.
Azt hiszem, hogy X, mert Y.
I think that X, because Y.

items.spanish: Szerintem ez a jobb terv, mert olcsóbb.
items.english: In my opinion this is the better plan, because it's cheaper.

items.spanish: Nem értek egyet, mert szerintem a másik étterem finomabb.
items.english: I don't agree, because in my opinion the other restaurant is tastier.

sections.content: Miért gondolod ezt? ("Why do you think that?") reuses miért exactly as you already know it — it's the natural follow-up question once someone has just given you their szerintem, azt hiszem, or gondolom.
